I can’t give a precise percentage for last quarter without the underlying data. I don’t have access to your systems or any source file to inspect, so any single-number answer would be a guess. (Stating uncertainty: I may be able to compute an exact value if you provide the counts or a dataset.)

If you want to compute it yourself or send the data, here’s what I need and how to compute it:

1) Clarify definitions
- Who counts as “users up for renewal”? (e.g., all active subscribers whose contracts/subscriptions expired last quarter)
- What counts as “renewed”? (e.g., renewed within the quarter, auto-renewals, partial renewals, upgrades)
- What date range is “last quarter”? (e.g., Q2 2026 = Apr 1–Jun 30, 2026)

2) Basic formula
Renewal rate (%) = (Number of users who renewed during the period / Number of users up for renewal during the period) × 100

3) Example (hypothetical)
- If 820 users were up for renewal and 656 renewed:
  Renewal rate = (656 / 820) × 100 ≈ 80.0%

4) Practical queries / formulas you can use
- SQL (example):
  SELECT
    SUM(CASE WHEN renewed = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS renewed_count,
    COUNT(*) AS up_for_renewal_count,
    100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN renewed = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*) AS renewal_rate_pct
  FROM subscriptions
  WHERE renewal_date BETWEEN '2026-04-01' AND '2026-06-30';

- Excel/Sheets:
  = (COUNTIFS(RenewalStatusRange, "Renewed", RenewalDateRange, ">=2026-04-01", RenewalDateRange, "<=2026-06-30") / COUNTIFS(RenewalDateRange, ">=2026-04-01", RenewalDateRange, "<=2026-06-30")) * 100

5) Caveats to consider
- Exclude new customers who weren’t up for renewal.
- Decide how to treat partial renewals, prorated renewals, or users who churned but re-subscribed within the quarter.
- If sample sizes are small, report confidence intervals or absolute counts alongside percentage.

References on renewal/retention metrics and standard definitions:
- Investopedia — Customer Retention Rate (definition and formula): https://www.investopedia.com/terms/c/customer-retention-rate.asp
- SaaS metrics guidance (renewal/retention concepts): https://www.forentrepreneurs.com/saas-metrics-2/ (David Skok)

If you paste the counts (users up for renewal and users who renewed) or upload a CSV/table with the relevant columns, I will calculate the precise renewal percentage for last quarter.
